title: Property Management CRM: Five Tools for Owner and Tenant Leads
html:
A property management CRM should hold two lead lists: property owners who might hire you, and renters who might lease a unit. Most firms pair a CRM such as LeadSimple or HubSpot with their accounting software, and add steady lead generation so both lists keep filling. Published plans in this guide run from free to $499 a month, and the page for each tool states one limit.

A property management CRM has to do three jobs: capture the lead, keep every conversation in one place and hand the account to operations. Property managers sell to two audiences. Owners decide who manages a building, and renters decide whether a unit gets filled. One system can serve both if the pipelines are kept apart.

This guide sorts five tools by the job each one does, with the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

Which property management CRM tracks owner and renter leads together?

LeadSimple is built for property managers and is the one tool in this guide that describes itself that way. It bundles a CRM with operations, phone, inbox and leasing tools.

  • LeadSimple: lists CRM, operations, phone and inbox, leasing, maintenance and AI tools, and works alongside property accounting software such as AppFolio, Buildium and Rent Manager. The One plan is $199 a month, month to month, with 50 doors, unlimited teammates and 2 CRM pipelines. One Max is $499 a month with 100 doors and unlimited pipelines. Limit: each extra active pipeline on One costs $30 a month, and the 14-day trial asks for a credit card.

The lists a lower rate on a 12-month agreement: $169 a month for One and $429 a month for One Max, billed monthly. The page does not describe how owner leads are sourced, so confirm in a demo that you can build a separate owner pipeline.

LeadSimple's One plan includes 500 calling minutes, 1,000 messaging credits and 50 AI voice minutes. A busy leasing desk should estimate its monthly calls and texts before it picks a plan. Phone and text use is where a flat price can stop being flat.

Two pipelines is the practical floor for a property manager. One tracks owners and one tracks renters. A firm that adds a third stream, such as vendor or investor contacts, hits the $30 add-on fast.

Which free CRM works for a small property management company?

HubSpot CRM is the free choice for a firm that needs a pipeline and a contact list before it needs property tools. It does not know what a unit or a lease is, so every property field is one you add.

  • HubSpot CRM: a general sales CRM that lists up to 1,000 contacts and one-to-one email on its Free plan. The Free plan is $0 for up to 2 users with no credit card. Starter starts at $7 per seat a month on annual billing, and the page's FAQ states $10 per seat month to month. Limit: the free plan caps at 2 users, and the page shows two Starter figures, so confirm the one you will pay.

A free CRM suits a manager who is growing a book of owners by phone and referral. Create a deal for each owner, add the unit count as a field and set a follow-up date. That is enough to stop a warm owner from going quiet.

Name your stages in plain words. Owner stages might be inquiry, call booked, proposal sent and signed. Move each lead one stage at a time so the report shows where owners stall.

Which property management software handles the leasing side without a separate CRM?

Buildium and TenantCloud both include leasing and communication tools inside their property management software, so a small firm can skip a standalone CRM at first.

  • Buildium: lists Essential at $65 a month, Growth at $202 a month and Premium at $420 a month, all shown as starting prices. Essential covers basic accounting, maintenance, leasing and communications. Limit: new customers on Growth or Premium must use Buildium's onboarding service, and the page does not state unit minimums or billing terms.
  • TenantCloud: lists Starter at $15 a month billed annually, Growth at $29 and Pro at $50. Starter includes online rent payments, maintenance, listings and applications for unlimited properties. Limit: Starter caps at 10 leases and 10 lead text messages, and excludes the owner portal. The page shows conflicting monthly prices, so check the vendor.

Neither tool replaces a sales pipeline for owner leads. They manage the units you already hold. Use them for renter inquiries and applications, and keep owner prospecting in a CRM.

Cost shapes the choice. TenantCloud's entry plan is far below Buildium's, but its lease cap means a growing firm outgrows it. Count your current leases before you pick, and leave room for the next year.

Which free tool helps owners find a property management company?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that puts your firm in Google Maps and local search. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, photos, reviews and phone number when an owner searches for property management nearby. Limit: it needs current photos, posts and review replies, and it does not track a lead after the call. See Google's Business Profile help page.

Owners read reviews before they call. If a bad review lands, read how to handle a negative review before you reply.

How do you choose a property management CRM?

Choose a property management CRM with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: can it run a separate pipeline for owner leads and renter leads? Does it connect to your accounting software?

Cost: add the plan price, extra pipelines, extra users and phone credits. Then compare the total against one year of management fees from a single owner.

Setup effort: can one person import contacts and build both pipelines in a weekend, or does the vendor need to onboard you?

A firm with a small portfolio can run HubSpot CRM for owner leads and TenantCloud Starter for renters. That stack lists at $15 a month on annual billing before add-ons. A larger firm on AppFolio or Buildium fits LeadSimple on top, because the page says it works alongside them.

Change one thing at a time. Add the CRM first, run it for a month and review the report before you add phone or AI features.

What should a property management CRM track for owner leads?

A property management CRM should track the owner's unit count, property type, current manager and the date of the last contact. Those four fields drive every sales decision.

  • Unit count and property type: a single-family owner and a 40-unit building need different proposals. Tag both so pricing stays consistent.
  • Current manager: an owner who already has a manager needs a reason to switch. Note the complaint they gave you.
  • Lead source: record whether the owner came from search, a referral or a map listing. Without it you cannot tell which channel is worth the budget.
  • Next step and date: every open owner lead needs one named action and a due date.

Keep an eye on the cost of ads against the fee one owner pays over a year.

How should a CRM hand an account to your property software?

Hand the account over at one clear moment: when the owner signs the management agreement or the renter signs the lease. Before that point the CRM owns the record, and after it the property software does.

  • Owner signed: create the owner and property in your accounting system, then mark the deal won in the CRM. Copy the unit count and fee terms across once.
  • Lease signed: the application and lease live in the property software. Close the lead in the CRM and stop sales reminders.
  • Lost lead: record the reason, such as price, timing or a competing manager. After a few months those reasons show you what to fix.
  • One owner per record: name one person who corrects a contact when details change, so two systems never disagree.

This handoff is where firms lose data. A weekly check of new owners against the accounting system takes minutes and catches a missed entry before a rent run.

If you use LeadSimple beside AppFolio, Buildium or Rent Manager, the vendor page says the tools work alongside each other. Ask for the exact sync steps in writing during the demo, because the page does not list them.

What should a property management CRM track for renter leads?

Track the move-in date, the unit type, the number of tours booked and the application status for each renter lead. Renter leads move fast and expire quickly.

  • Move-in date: a lead that needs a unit in two weeks gets a call first.
  • Unit match: note the beds, baths and budget so you can send two or three matching units.
  • Tour status: mark whether a tour is booked, done or missed, and set a reminder for the missed ones.
  • Application status: link the lead to the application so nobody asks the same question twice.

Buildium and TenantCloud both hold applications, so use their records for this stage. Keep the CRM for the first reply and the follow-up. When the renter applies, the property software owns the record.

How do you follow up property management leads without losing them?

Reply to every lead the same business day, and write down who owns each stage. Without an owner, a lead sits in the CRM until it goes cold.

  • Owners get a call: an owner choosing a manager wants a person, so call first and email a summary after.
  • Renters get a text: a renter is often browsing several listings, so a quick text with a tour link works better than a voicemail.
  • Set a second touch: every open lead gets a reminder date, so a quiet lead gets one more contact before it closes.
  • Review the pipeline weekly: a ten-minute check of stalled leads catches problems early.

Leads need a source worth following up. Search ads from property management Google Ads and rankings from property management SEO bring owners to the site.

A new website also needs a clear inquiry form that feeds the CRM.

What is the best CRM for property management?

There is no single best pick, because it depends on your size and accounting software. LeadSimple is built for property managers, HubSpot CRM is free for up to 2 users, and Buildium and TenantCloud bundle leasing tools. Test each one against your own owner and renter workflow.

How much does a property management CRM cost?

Published plans in this guide run from free for HubSpot CRM to $499 a month for LeadSimple One Max. TenantCloud Starter lists at $15 a month on annual billing, and Buildium Essential starts at $65 a month. Check each vendor before you decide, because add-ons raise the total.

Is HubSpot CRM free for property managers?

Yes, for a small team. HubSpot lists a Free plan at $0 for up to 2 users with no credit card required. It lists up to 1,000 contacts and one-to-one email. It has no unit, lease or rent features, so pair it with property software.

Does a property management company need a CRM and property software?

Often both. Property software such as Buildium or TenantCloud manages units, leases and rent, while a CRM manages the sales pipeline for owners and renters. A small firm can start with property software alone and add a CRM when owner leads need follow-up.

Does LeadSimple replace AppFolio or Buildium?

No. LeadSimple states that it works alongside property accounting software such as AppFolio, Buildium and Rent Manager. It adds CRM, phone, inbox and leasing tools, so keep your accounting system and use LeadSimple for the sales and communication side of the business.

Should owner leads and renter leads share one pipeline?

No. Owners and renters have different stages, timelines and values. Keep two pipelines so each report shows how long each group takes to close. LeadSimple's One plan includes 2 CRM pipelines, and extra active pipelines cost $30 a month each.

How fast should a property manager reply to a new lead?

Reply the same business day, and call an owner lead first. For renters, send a text with a tour link soon after the inquiry. Both groups often contact several firms, so a quick, clear reply gives you the best chance at the next step.

note the beds, baths and budget so you can send two or three matching units.
-
Tour status:
mark whether a tour is booked, done or missed, and set a reminder for the missed ones.
-
Application status:
link the lead to the application so nobody asks the same question twice.
Buildium and TenantCloud both hold applications, so use their records for this stage. Keep the CRM for the first reply and the follow-up. When the renter applies, the property software owns the record.
##
How do you follow up property management leads without losing them?
Reply to every lead the same business day, and write down who owns each stage. Without an owner, a lead sits in the CRM until it goes cold.
-
Owners get a call:
an owner choosing a manager wants a person, so call first and email a summary after.
-
Renters get a text:
a renter is often browsing several listings, so a quick text with a tour link works better than a voicemail.
-
Set a second touch:
every open lead gets a reminder date, so a quiet lead gets one more contact before it closes.
-
Review the pipeline weekly:
a ten-minute check of stalled leads catches problems early.
Leads need a source worth following up. Search ads from property management Google Ads and rankings from property management SEO bring owners to the site.
A new website also needs a clear inquiry form that feeds the CRM.
###
What is the best CRM for property management?
There is no single best pick, because it depends on your size and accounting software. LeadSimple is built for property managers, HubSpot CRM is free for up to 2 users, and Buildium and TenantCloud bundle leasing tools. Test each one against your own owner and renter workflow.
###
How much does a property management CRM cost?
Published plans in this guide run from free for HubSpot CRM to $499 a month for LeadSimple One Max. TenantCloud Starter lists at $15 a month on annual billing, and Buildium Essential starts at $65 a month. Check each vendor before you decide, because add-ons raise the total.
###
Is HubSpot CRM free for property managers?
Yes, for a small team. HubSpot lists a Free plan at $0 for up to 2 users with no credit card required. It lists up to 1,000 contacts and one-to-one email. It has no unit, lease or rent features, so pair it with property software.
###
Does a property management company need a CRM and property software?
Often both. Property software such as Buildium or TenantCloud manages units, leases and rent, while a CRM manages the sales pipeline for owners and renters. A small firm can start with property software alone and add a CRM when owner leads need follow-up.
###
Does LeadSimple replace AppFolio or Buildium?
No. LeadSimple states that it works alongside property accounting software such as AppFolio, Buildium and Rent Manager. It adds CRM, phone, inbox and leasing tools, so keep your accounting system and use LeadSimple for the sales and communication side of the business.
###
Should owner leads and renter leads share one pipeline?
No. Owners and renters have different stages, timelines and values. Keep two pipelines so each report shows how long each group takes to close. LeadSimple's One plan includes 2 CRM pipelines, and extra active pipelines cost $30 a month each.
###
How fast should a property manager reply to a new lead?
Reply the same business day, and call an owner lead first. For renters, send a text with a tour link soon after the inquiry. Both groups often contact several firms, so a quick, clear reply gives you the best chance at the next step.
